stories.headline: Rep. Gabe Evans to run in Colorado's 4th District in 2028 after losing 8th District seat
stories.summary:
Republican Rep. Gabe Evans announced Monday that he will run for Colorado's 4th Congressional District in 2028. He lost his 8th District seat this year to Democrat Manny Rutinel, a former state representative, who won by 15 percentage points. The 8th District spans Denver's northern suburbs into Greeley and was drawn in 2021 to be a tossup.

Evans, a former state legislator, Denver-area police officer and 12-year Army veteran, lives in Fort Lupton. His campaign said he starts the 2028 cycle with $300,000 in cash on hand and strong name recognition after one of the most expensive congressional races of the cycle.

The 4th District includes Douglas County and much of the Eastern Plains. Rep. Lauren Boebert, who represented it, lost to Democrat Eileen Laubacher and told Scripps News last week that she would not seek to run again. It is unclear whether Evans's early announcement will deter other Republicans from entering the race, given the few opportunities for Republicans to win in Colorado.

stories.headline: Nuggets fall to Suns 117-105 as shooting and rebounding problems resurface
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets fell to 7-5 on the 2026-27 season with a 117-105 loss to the Phoenix Suns at Ball Arena on Monday night. It was Phoenix's first road win of the year.

Devin Booker scored 20 points for the Suns, and seven Phoenix players finished in double figures. Denver struggled from beyond the arc, shooting 9-for-30 on 3-pointers.

Nikola Jokic had little rebounding help, and he addressed the team's mistakes after the game. The loss exposed shooting and rebounding troubles that have surfaced before for the Nuggets this season.

stories.headline: Arrest made in Sterling Ranch hit-and-run that seriously injured child on bike
stories.summary:
The Douglas County Sheriff's Office announced Monday that deputies arrested a driver accused of hitting a child on a bicycle in the Sterling Ranch area and leaving the scene. The crash happened Friday.

Investigators determined the child was riding in a bike lane when a vehicle entered the lane, struck the bicyclist and fled without stopping.

The child was seriously injured but is expected to survive. The sheriff's office released the arrest information in a press release Monday morning.

stories.headline: Colorado directs $400,000 Dollar General settlement to food assistance programs
stories.summary:
The Colorado Attorney General's Office announced Monday that it is directing $400,000 in settlement money from a consumer protection case against Dollar General to food assistance programs. The investigation found the chain was charging customers higher prices at the register than those advertised on store shelves.

The state reached the settlement in October 2025. It also required the company to increase its reporting requirements and give the state regular audit reports. Last week, the state reached a similar settlement with Family Dollar over register prices that exceeded advertised prices in store, online and on its mobile app.

The money has been distributed as grants to hunger relief organizations statewide, with 56% going to rural and frontier communities. The grants paid for refrigeration equipment, food storage and transportation. A $5,000 grant helped the Community Hub Food Mini Market at Swansea Elementary in Denver buy a freezer, refrigerators and shelving. Feeding Colorado helped distribute the grants. Attorney General Phil Weiser, who becomes governor in January, said the funding is helping families across the state.

stories.headline: RTD begins $12 million planning phase for unfinished N Line extension
stories.summary:
The Regional Transportation District has launched a project development phase for the unfinished FasTracks N Line extension in northern Adams County, including Thornton. Up to $12 million will fund environmental review, corridor validation and preliminary engineering for the final 5.5 miles north of the Eastlake-124th station to Highway 7.

The work follows RTD board approval of the funding and a partnership framework with Adams County. RTD's 2025 report estimates the remaining capital cost at $395.7 million in 2024 dollars and projects 1,500 daily boardings by 2045. The existing line carries about 3,600 weekday riders.

The $12 million is part of an estimated $55 million for pre-construction activities, and construction funding has not been identified. The phase is expected to last about two years. Completing all four remaining FasTracks corridors would cost about $1.6 billion, with roughly $443 million in potential funding identified. The Independence Institute's Randal O'Toole criticized the continued push for rail over bus transit.

stories.headline: Three finalists vie to lead Aurora's new public safety oversight office
stories.summary:
Three finalists are competing to become Aurora's first Manager of Public Safety Accountability: John Hummel, Shenandoah Titus and Eric Williams. The manager will lead a new independent oversight office created by a unanimous City Council vote this summer, as the city's consent decree winds down.

The civilian role is meant to build transparency and public trust after the 2019 death of Elijah McClain. A community meet and greet with the candidates was held Monday night, and a community advisory committee developed standardized questions based on community submissions.

Williams, an Aurora native, is a deputy vice president at the U.S. Center for SafeSport and a former deputy director of Denver's Department of Public Safety and FBI investigator. Titus founded Police Oversight USA and has more than two decades of oversight experience. Hummel is a Denver litigation attorney and a former elected district attorney in Deschutes County, Oregon.

stories.headline: Man charged with murder in Glendale apartment shooting extradited from Mexico
stories.summary:
A man charged with murder in a shooting at a metro Denver apartment complex has been extradited back to Colorado after fleeing to Mexico, according to a Glendale Police Department arrest affidavit.

The case stems from a shooting at an apartment complex in Glendale, an enclave surrounded by Denver.

The affidavit details the suspect's flight to Mexico and his return to Colorado to face the murder charge.

stories.headline: Greater Arvada Chamber names Kelly Caufield new CEO and president
stories.summary:
The Greater Arvada Chamber of Commerce has named Kelly Caufield, former executive director of the Common Sense Institute Colorado, as its new CEO and president. Board chair Lindsay Reinert said the board sought a leader who could build on the chamber's foundation while bringing a fresh perspective.

Caufield holds a master's degree in public policy from George Washington University. She said her priorities include helping businesses stay rooted in Arvada and connecting them with a skilled workforce.

The item was part of a roundup of metro business openings. Joy Batch Cookies & Coffee opened in the Highlands Ranch Town Center, owned by Sarah Carlson. French Florist, a flower shop franchise, opened its first Denver location at 6300 E. Hampden Ave. last month, run by siblings Hayley and Dustin Tatley.

stories.headline: Life Time to open $60 million club in Castle Pines on Nov. 18
stories.summary:
Life Time will open a $60 million, 102,600-square-foot club in Castle Pines on Nov. 18. The club anchors the Canyonside development.

The facility features a new, more efficient design layout, according to the Denver Business Journal. The opening adds a major health and athletic club to the Douglas County community.

stories.headline: Denver pot accessory firm Blazy Susan opening manufacturing plant
stories.summary:
Blazy Susan, the Denver-based cannabis accessory company, is opening a manufacturing plant in Denver.

The firm was named to Inc. magazine's list of the 100 fastest-growing private companies in 2023.

The plant represents an expansion for the company's local operations.

stories.headline: Denver priest facing parishioner petition to take sabbatical before reassignment
stories.summary:
A Denver priest whose parishioners petitioned for his ouster last year announced he will take a six-month sabbatical. He will then be reassigned to a new parish.

The move comes with the encouragement and support of Denver's recently installed Archbishop James Golka. The priest is Rev. Daniel Ciucci of Most Precious Blood.

The announcement follows a year of tension at the parish over his leadership.

topStory.headline: Trump Arrives in Manila for Quad Talks and ASEAN Summit Ahead of Thursday Meeting With Xi and Putin in Shenzhen
topStory.summary:
President Trump arrived Tuesday in the Philippines to begin a multiday trip through Asia. After landing in Manila, he met with leaders of the Quad nations, Australia, India and Japan, a grouping with the United States that has sought to counter China's influence in the Asia-Pacific region. Mr. Trump described the relationship as "very special" and announced an $85 million investment in artificial intelligence software, which he called the "greatest opportunity for economic growth since the Industrial Revolution." Protesters gathered in Manila ahead of the visit, carrying "Trump Out" signs and urging the public to reject an AI hub named Pax Silica.

The centerpiece of the trip is a meeting Thursday in Shenzhen, China, among Mr. Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, the first such meeting among the three leaders. The White House said the talks are expected to center on reducing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. Mr. Trump said Monday the leaders would discuss denuclearization, which he called a "tough subject," as well as Iran and Ukraine, although an official said over the weekend that Ukraine was not expected to be discussed. Mr. Trump also said he may meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China, saying after arriving that Kim "would like to" come but "we'll see what happens."

In Manila, the president is attending the annual Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit. His schedule includes a trade deal signing with Thailand and a dinner with Southeast Asian and other regional leaders. On Wednesday he is to hold a state visit and lunch banquet with Philippine President Bongbong Marcos at the presidential palace before departing for Shenzhen. There he will meet with leaders on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, which will bring together leaders from almost two dozen economies. Elon Musk is expected to accompany the president but will not take part in the meeting with Putin and Xi, according to a senior White House official.

Mr. Trump acknowledged that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have "two lines of thought" on how to handle China, saying they "handled that very well." The trip follows Mr. Trump's visit to China in May for a summit with Xi, where he promoted "fantastic trade deals" and acknowledged a shared desire to end the U.S.-Iran conflict. Xi visited the United States in September, his first White House visit in more than a decade.

The trip comes as the wars in Iran and Ukraine remain in focus and as domestic political pressures grow at home. Vice President JD Vance said this week that Republicans paid a political cost in the midterm elections from higher gas and energy prices tied to the Iran conflict, while saying there is no daylight between him and the president on the war. Thursday's three-way meeting will be closely watched for any movement on nuclear arms issues and the Iran conflict.
